title: Uniform filtration restriction of the filtered homotopy category and its cone localization
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Start with the bounded-below homotopy category of complexes of finite filtered objects, with its filtered maps, filtered homotopies and graded quasi-isomorphisms [def-trf-finite-filtered-localization]. Let $B$ be either no prescribed interval or a prescribed pair $(a,b)$. In that existing category impose the condition that there exist integers $c\le d$ with $F^cK^n=K^n$ and $F^{d+1}K^n=0$ for every cochain degree $n$, independently of $n$. Optionally impose in addition the existence of an integer $N$ with $K^n=0$ for $n>N$. Denote the corresponding full subcategories by $K_{F,B}^{+}(\mathcal A)$ and $K_{F,B}^{b}(\mathcal A)$ respectively. Their triangles and shifts are inherited from the filtered cone triangulation [def-weil-triangulated-category]: these conditions contain zero, are stable under integer shifts, and are closed under distinguished triangles up to isomorphism, so Mathlib's full-subcategory triangulation applies. In either category let $W$ be the inverse image of the existing graded quasi-isomorphisms under its full inclusion. This class has a left calculus of fractions and is compatible with that inherited triangulation. Define $D_{F,B}^{+}(\mathcal A)$ and $D_{F,B}^{b}(\mathcal A)$ to be the formal localizations at these respective classes $W$, with the standard triangulated localization structure. All bounds prescribed by $B$ are retained. These are a homotopy-category model of the localizations, constructed by restricting the existing filtered homotopy category; no new filtration, filtered homotopy relation or graded map is introduced.
